summary: Final results are in, with Netanyahu's camp ahead but short of a majority; Herzog receives the official results and opens consultations with the factions on Wednesday, Nov 4, and the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10. Together and the Democrats will recommend Eisenkot, the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to as well, and Tibi says change is impossible without the Arab parties, while Liberman has yet to commit and is due to speak after his faction meets on Monday. Likud says it opposes a rotation and has questioned the election's integrity after the elections committee chief said the vote was properly run, and Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu is preparing for a new election. UTJ remains the swing party, with unnamed senior figures floating outside support for an Eisenkot government.

phase.now: Final results published; consultations confirmed to open Wednesday, Nov 4, once Herzog receives the official results
phase.next: Herzog will ask each faction whom it recommends and then choose a candidate for the mandate; the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners, whom he told they are staying together. Without a majority, Netanyahu needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu rather than join him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman told party members on Oct 29 that his pledge not to sit with the Haredi parties stands.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election.

blockers.text: Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Likud whip Ofir Katz said on Nov 1 the party opposes rotation and that others may join on the basis of the existing coalition.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: After meeting Lapid on Oct 31, Eisenkot said any MK accepting his four principles could be a partner, and vowed to use a Knesset majority for a state inquiry, national service and repealing judicial-overhaul laws.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Together announced on Nov 1 it will recommend Eisenkot for prime minister, saying Bennett is respecting the voters' decision and has informed Eisenkot.

אמת.stance: On Nov 1 Golan said Netanyahu should not lead another Iran war and urged forming an alternative government quickly; he has backed including Arab parties since the election.

ל.stance: Liberman has not said whether he will recommend Eisenkot and plans to speak after his faction meets on Nov 2; in an X post over the weekend he again refused to rely on Arab parties.

שס.stance: Unnamed Haredi sources say Deri has ruled out an opposition-led government without Likud and would join a unity government only alongside Likud.

ג.stance: Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party may support an Eisenkot-led government from outside without first passing a draft law, though Asher had said UTJ would not join a government without one.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir attacked the idea of a government with the Joint List after Jabareen declined to call Hamas a terror group; he rejects unity with Eisenkot and backs keeping a right-wing government.

ט.stance: Smotrich met Netanyahu in person on Oct 29, Ynet reports, and says the Arab party heads should be questioned by the Shin Bet over alleged foreign funding.

עם.stance: Abbas denies any link to the alleged foreign interference, pledges full cooperation with investigators and accuses Netanyahu of inciting against Arab citizens; he has said he'd join a government that tackles crime and discrimination.

ודם.stance: Tibi told Channel 12 the Arab parties are essential to any change and he wants to help bring down the government without seeking a ministry; he has said the Joint List will recommend Eisenkot but stay outside the government.
